notes.verdict: The Lancet retracted the SCIPIO trial report in 2019 after Harvard's investigation found unreliable data. The 2011 entry still presents it as a breakthrough.
notes.section: Two retracted sources (SCIPIO stem-cell trial; skin-to-neuron paper)
notes.text:
Two entries on this page cite papers that have since been retracted:
* November: "A study of heart failure patients treated with their own stem cells has achieved striking results..." cites the SCIPIO trial report in ''The Lancet'' ([https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(11)61590-0 doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(11)61590-0]), retracted on 14 March 2019 ([https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(19)30542-2 retraction notice]) after a Harvard investigation found its data unreliable.
* August: "Bypassing stem cells, scientists have made neurons directly from human skin" cites ''Directed Conversion of Alzheimer's Disease Patient Skin Fibroblasts Into Functional Neurons'' in ''Cell'' ([https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2011.07.007 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2011.07.007]), retracted on 10 April 2014 ([https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2014.03.002 retraction notice]).
Both can stay as history, but readers should be told the results were retracted. Suggest adding a short note to each entry or marking the citations with {{tl|Retracted}}. (Disclosure: I found these with a tracker of retracted papers that I run.) ~~~~
